title: Fluidized Bed Combustor
model_title: Bubbling Fluidised Bed Combustor (with In-Bed Tubes & Cyclone)

introduction.definition: A bubbling fluidised bed combustor burns fuel inside a hot bed of sand fluidised by air blown up through a distributor. The well-mixed, hot bed burns low-grade or variable fuels completely at a moderate temperature; in-bed tubes raise steam, and a cyclone returns fines to the bed.
key_points: Bed ~ 800–900 °C: low NOx, in-bed sulphur capture with limestone
introduction.summary: A bubbling fluidised bed combustor burns fuel inside a hot bed of sand kept fluidised by air blown through a distributor. The hot, well-mixed bed burns low-grade and variable fuels at a moderate, uniform temperature; tubes in the bed and walls raise steam, and a cyclone returns fines to the bed.

temperature.title: Low, uniform combustion temperature
temperature.description: The bed is kept at roughly 800–900 °C — hot enough to burn the fuel completely but low enough to limit thermal NOx and to let limestone added to the bed capture sulphur. The large mass of hot sand gives stable combustion even of wet, low-grade or variable fuels.

video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Combustor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Fluidized Bed Combustor.
A bubbling fluidised bed combustor burns fuel inside a hot bed of sand fluidised by air blown up through a distributor.
The well-mixed, hot bed burns low-grade or variable fuels completely at a moderate temperature; in-bed tubes raise steam, and a cyclone returns fines to the bed.
Typical applications include biomass and waste-to-energy boilers; low-grade coal and lignite; sludge incineration.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Combustor Shell, Refractory Lining & Wind Box (below distributor).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Combustor — Operation

script.narration: How the Fluidized Bed Combustor works.
Fluidising air enters the wind box.
The distributor nozzles spread air across the bed.
Fuel drops into the bubbling sand bed and burns.
In-bed tubes absorb heat.
The cyclone returns fines; flue gas goes to heat recovery.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The bed is kept at roughly 800–900 °C — hot enough to burn the fuel completely but low enough to limit thermal NOx and to let limestone added to the bed capture sulphur.

video_tutorials.title: Fluidized Bed Combustor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Fluidized Bed Combustor.
Monitor bed temperature and ΔP.
Drain bed ash; check nozzles.
Inspect in-bed tubes for erosion; refractory.
Watch for bed agglomeration: defluidisation, hot spots. Common cause: alkali-rich fuels, high temperature.
Watch for tube erosion: thinning. Common cause: bed particle impact.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
